classification.difficultyReason: Express both parallel sides and the height using one variable, substitute into the familiar trapezium-area formula, factorise and reject the negative length.

content.prompt:
Use a quadratic equation to solve the problem. Clearly define any pronumerals introduced into your solution.

One of the parallel sides of a trapezium is 5 cm longer than the other, and its height is half the length of the shorter parallel side. If the area is $225\text{ cm}^2$, find the lengths of the parallel sides.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the length of the shorter parallel side. The longer parallel side is $(x+5)$ cm and the height is $\frac{x}{2}$ cm.

Using $A=\frac12(a+b)h$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac12\bigl(x+(x+5)\bigr)\frac{x}{2}&=225\\x(2x+5)&=900\\2x^2+5x-900&=0\\(x-20)(2x+45)&=0\end{align*}$$

Thus $x=20$ or $x=-\frac{45}{2}$. A length must be positive, so $x=20$.

The parallel sides have lengths $20\text{ cm}$ and $20+5=25\text{ cm}$.
